plan: Given my value of $15, I aim to maximize profit by bidding slightly above the expected third-highest bid. Since all values are equally likely between $0 and $49, the average bid is $24.5. A rational strategy is to bid slightly above this average, but not exceeding my value. I'll bid $15, as bidding higher risks negative profit if I win. This bid balances the chance of winning with potential profit.

Given my value of $36, I aim to bid slightly above the expected average bid to maximize profit while minimizing risk. Assuming values are uniformly distributed, the average value is $24.5. Rational bidders would bid near their value, so I will bid slightly above this average to outbid those with lower values but still below my value to ensure profit if I win. I will bid $30 to balance competitiveness and profit potential.

My value for the prize is $42. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly below my value to ensure a win while minimizing payment. Given rational bidders, others will bid close to their values. I will bid $41.9, slightly below my value, to outbid others who may bid close to their values but not exceed them. This maximizes my chance of winning while paying less than my value, ensuring a positive profit.
